title: Finite positive-mass tube lower-bound interface and coarse scaling boundary
question: What exact finite Gibbs-mass lower bound follows from the existing R-464/R-465 comparison when a measurable positive-volume branch tube and an energy ceiling are supplied?
purpose: Turn the positive-mass tube prerequisite into a quantitative, auditable interface without changing the established A6, T-054, T-059, or T-061 methods.

exact_scope.domain: finite spectral Galerkin space with m=(2N+1)^3 sites and d=6m real coordinates
exact_scope.tube: B_N(c,delta)=c+[-delta,delta]^d with delta>0 and measurable embedding supplied by a later owner
exact_scope.partition_upper: Z_N(beta)<=Z_upper_N(beta) from the R-465 radial comparison
exact_scope.energy_ceiling: F_N(z)<=E_tube for every z in B_N
exact_scope.uniformity_test: A nonvanishing tube mass would require liminf_N L_N(beta)>-infinity; this is not asserted
exact_scope.fixtures: owner-neutral delta=1/16 and E_tube=1 over N=[1,2,3,4,6,8,10], beta=[1/2,1,2]

theorem.positive_volume: delta>0 implies the box tube has strictly positive Lebesgue volume
theorem.finite_lower_bound: A tube energy ceiling and an R-465 partition upper bound imply the displayed finite Gibbs-mass lower bound
theorem.log_decomposition: The lower-bound logarithm separates geometric volume, Boltzmann ceiling, and comparison normalization
theorem.scaling_boundary: For the declared fixed-width owner-neutral fixtures, the coarse lower log is finite and strictly decreases with cutoff; no uniform conclusion follows

proof_skeleton: Retain the R-464/R-465 lower-energy and upper-partition comparisons.
Use the supplied pointwise energy ceiling to lower-bound the Boltzmann integral over a measurable box tube.
Use the exact d-dimensional box volume and divide by the R-465 upper partition envelope.
Audit the resulting log budget and its cutoff trend without promoting it to a uniform probability or entropy theorem.
Run non-importing independent, hostile, integrated, and Lean checks.
assumptions: The R-464 sextic comparison and R-465 radial partition upper envelope are valid at each fixed cutoff.
A later owner supplies a measurable branch embedding and a valid pointwise energy ceiling on its tube.
The half-width and energy ceiling in this packet are declared audit fixtures, not fitted or physical values.
missing_assumptions: A source-owned active-branch embedding and positive-mass tube tied to R-461/R-463.
An actual correlated partition normalization with cutoff- and volume-uniform bounds.
A branch-relative entropy/Jacobian compensator, tightness, floor removal, and ordered continuum limits.
A source-owned Q3LOCK dynamics, physical branch, QFT/Yang--Mills identity, or mass-gap bridge.

adversarial_review.check: Could the d-dimensional volume lose a coordinate?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by exact volume identity and hostile mutation.
REJECTED by the declared side identity.

adversarial_review.check: Could the upper partition comparison be used in reverse?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by the ratio inequality and hostile mutation.

adversarial_review.check: Could synthetic fixtures be called a source-owned branch?
Can finite decreasing rows be called a uniform mass theorem?
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD-REJECTED; only the liminf criterion is recorded.

adversarial_review.check: Can an exact zero-mass branch be conditioned by this box formula?
Does this interface replace an existing method or owner order?
adversarial_review.disposition: DISMISSED; it is an additive R-464/R-465 consequence.

evidence_level: T0 exact finite conditional Gibbs-mass lower-bound interface with owner-neutral box fixtures
non_claims: The owner-neutral box is not a source-owned active branch and does not select a physical sector.
The finite lower bound is conditional on an energy ceiling and is not cutoff-uniform.
The decreasing coarse log bound diagnoses the present full-dimensional comparison; it is not a no-go theorem for branch-relative normalization.
No entropy density, tightness, floor removal, continuum, Pre-A, Sector-A, QFT, Yang--Mills or mass-gap conclusion follows.
Existing T-054 forward, T-059/T-061 inverse methods, owner order and promotion firewalls are unchanged.
boundary: R-466 supplies only a fixed-cutoff conditional tube-mass lower-bound interface. The owner embedding, actual energy ceiling, correlated partition asymptotic, entropy/Jacobian compensator, uniformity, tightness, limits, and physical identity remain open.
next_action: Hash-pin a source-owned active-branch embedding, measurable tube and energy ceiling; instantiate R-466 with R-463's metric and test a branch-relative entropy/Jacobian compensator without repeating the full-dimensional proxy.
